simple.meaning: שֶׁלַח (shelach) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a missile of attack, i.e. spear ; also (figuratively) a shoot of growth; i.e. branch.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 2 Chronicles 23:10. The surrounding context includes altar, kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שֶׁלַח (H7973) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

timeline.evidenceText: He set all the people, every man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, near the altar and the house, around the king.

He took courage, built up all the wall that was broken down, and raised it up to the towers, with the other wall outside, and strengthened Millo in David’s city, and made weapons and shields in abundance.
Our adversaries said, “They will not know or see, until we come in among them and kill them, and cause the work to cease.”
Those who built the wall, and those who bore burdens loaded themselves; everyone with one of his hands did the work, and with the other held his weapon.
He keeps back his soul from the pit,
But if they don’t listen, they will perish by the sword;

definitions.full: H7973. shelach I. שֶׁ֫לַח noun [masculine] missile, weapon, sprout (late); — absolute ׳שׁ Joel 2:8 +, שָׁ֑לַח Neh 4:11 ; Job 33:18 , suffix שִׁלְחוֺ Neh 4:17 ; plural שְׁלָחִים 2Chr 23:10 , etc.; — 1 missile, weapon , Neh 4:11 and 4:17 (where הַמַּיִם corrupt; read probably בִּימִינוֺ or בְּיָדוֺ ; see Ryle BeRy Berthol), 2Chr 23:10 (distinguished from מָנֵן חֲנִית, ); collective 32:5 and בַּשׁ ׳עָבַר Job 33:18 ; 36:12 ( perish by or < rush upon [and perish]), Joel 2:8 (see בְּעַד ). 2 sprout, shoot (compare [ שְׁלוּחָה ], and √ Psa 80:12 ; Jer 17:8 ), מַּרְדֵּס שְׁלָחַיִךְ Song 4:13 (figurative; meaning ? Perles Anal. 63 proposes לְחָיָיִךְ שְׁנֵי thy two cheeks ); + probably Ezek 31:5 (read בִּשְׁלָחָיו Co Toy and others, or בְּשִׁלְחֵי [with 31:6 ] Krae).
